# Kyoto 5-Day Trip Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg

A relaxed Kyoto plan for **2 adults** from **2025-10-14 to 2025-10-18** with a **$900 sightseeing budget** excluding flights.
Built around **temples, food markets, one museum, minimal walking, and no starts before 9:00 AM**.
Media: Alt=Built around **temples, food markets, one museum, minimal walking, and no starts before 9:00 AM**, Kyoto, Japan

## Daily Itinerary by Area
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Day
Media: Alt=Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Day, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Arrive, check in, late breakfast near Kyoto Station or Gion
- Afternoon: Kiyomizu-dera, then a slow stroll through Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka
- Evening: Dinner in Gion; optional Yasaka Shrine night visit
- Pace: Mostly taxi/bus between stops to keep walking light

Day 2: Central Kyoto Temples + Museum
Media: Alt=Day 2: Central Kyoto Temples + Museum, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Start after 9:00 AM at Nijo Castle
- Afternoon: Kyoto National Museum for your one museum stop, then Sanjusangendo
- Evening: Pontocho or Kawaramachi for an easy dinner
- Pace: Good transit day; use short taxi hops where helpful

Day 3: Market Morning + Northern Temples
Media: Alt=Day 3: Market Morning + Northern Temples, Kyoto, Japan
- Morning: Nishiki Market for food tasting and snacks
- Afternoon: Kinkaku-ji, then Ryoan-ji if energy allows
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for a relaxed meal
- Pace: Market is easy on walking; temples work well by bus/taxi

Day 4: Arashiyama Scenic Day
- Morning: Late start, then Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Tenryu-ji
- Afternoon: River area, optional short boat ride or café break
- Evening: Dinner back in central Kyoto
- Pace: Keep it selective; skip extra side paths if you want less walking

Day 5: Fushimi + Departure Buffer
- Morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha after 9:00 AM, only the lower gates if you want minimal walking
- Afternoon: Fushimi sake district or a final lunch stop
- Evening: Pack, transfer, depart
- Pace: Best as a short temple-focused final day

## Kyoto Area Grouping Map
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- **Higashiyama / Gion**: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka, Yasaka Shrine
- **Central Kyoto**: Nijo Castle, Kyoto National Museum, Sanjusangendo, Pontocho
- **Downtown / Nishiki**: Nishiki Market, Kawaramachi dining
- **North Kyoto**: Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji
- **West Kyoto / Arashiyama**: Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, river area
- **South Kyoto / Fushimi**: Fushimi Inari Taisha, sake district

## Sightseeing Budget Breakdown
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Temple and shrine entry | $140 | Mix of paid and free sites |
| Museum and castle entry | $45 | Includes one museum plus Nijo Castle |
| Food markets and snacks | $180 | Nishiki Market, café stops, light tastings |
| Lunches and dinners | $220 | Comfortable mid-range meals for 2 |
| Local transport | $110 | Subway, bus, and a few taxis for low-walk days |
| Tea, sweets, and extras | $85 | Matcha, desserts, small souvenirs |
| Buffer | $120 | Weather, upgrades, or a taxi when needed |

## Budget Fit Check
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

- **Total planned sightseeing spend:** **$900**
- **Best value-saving lever:** use taxis only for short transfers on temple-heavy days
- **Best comfort-saving lever:** keep Arashiyama and Fushimi Inari to the most iconic sections only
